about: Per-query routing snapshot (tests/e2e/test_routing_snapshot.py). Update deliberately with: uv run python -m tests.e2e.routing_snapshot --write --reason "..."
history: per-query routing snapshot: scores resolve() actually used (base/penalty/adj diagnostics, no crash on drift), co-dependency groups, signal/tie-break detail, reality-check fit, and field-keyed consolidation records (#497)
#487: OpenSearch no longer wins non-search reads (base-score inflation and the ungated text_search override both fixed) -- its queries move to the committed engine that actually fits them.

#500 round 2 (review): the pattern-match bonus and its 100-point cap are removed outright -- #302 scores every query from its own tables only. This both reshapes which queries move (no more cap-driven exact ties decided by the source-compatible tie rule) and interacts with reality check's own per-query fit scoring, so Aurora PostgreSQL's share drops relative to #487 instead of rising.

#501: re-check every surviving engine after partial consolidation against the TRUE committed set, and never move a query to an engine that scores it lower than the one it is already on. wordpress: DocumentDB's 21-query share (an evaluation-order artifact) drops to 4 genuinely-justified queries; 17 move to Aurora MySQL or DynamoDB. discourse: DocumentDB keeps 183 of its 194 queries -- the never-worse rule finds no committed engine scores them as well; only 11 move to Aurora PostgreSQL.

#502 review correction: removed the min_fit score floor on consolidation moves and replaced it with a never-pad-to-justify rule (an engine's own re-check uses only its native queries, never anything another engine's consolidation redistributed onto it this run). wordpress: DocumentDB is now fully removed (7 of its 8 queries move to Aurora MySQL, 1 to DynamoDB, some at a lower score than DocumentDB's own -- accepted, since DocumentDB itself was never justified). discourse: unchanged from #500 -- the earlier 183-query DocumentDB retention was entirely an artifact of the now-removed score floor, not a real finding.

#502 redesign: two phases -- settle the committed engine set from native queries alone (order-independent), then place every query by the resolver's own per-query scores. wordpress collapses to a single owner engine (aurora_mysql); discourse keeps two (aurora_postgresql, dynamodb) with dynamodb's share rising to 40.1% since DocumentDB's former queries are now placed by the resolver's own scores, not reality check's separate scorer.

#502: Phase 1 settles the committed engine set with the resolver's own per-query scores, removing one worst-ranked candidate per round against a frozen snapshot; Phase 2 places every query via the same shared eligibility rule. Wordpress: DocumentDB removed, DynamoDB and Aurora MySQL both keep real shares (was a single-owner collapse in the prior draft). Discourse: Aurora PostgreSQL/DynamoDB/DocumentDB keep real shares.

#503: ties are now a structured, counted field (tied_engines); a tied query counts as native evidence for the one engine the placeholder already picked, re-resolved among surviving tied engines in Phase 2 (fixes a crash/weak-engine-drop when every query on an engine was tied); eligibility treats every tied engine as current so a placeholder's own pick never biases a gate; wording uses display names with no raw code or internal reference

#503 round 3: Phase 2's co-dependency group tie-break now seeds with sorted member ids (not whichever member comes first in trace order), matching the resolver and the floor; fixed heading pluralization and a broken consolidation-reason fragment; a cleared tie's reason now says which engine stopped qualifying

fix(referee): #485 -- documentdb gains the inverted_index capability (unindexed $regex scan, same position as Aurora MySQL's unindexed LIKE), so the hard gate stops scoring it 0 on leading-wildcard/full-text queries
Add the synthetic SQL Server sample, trailgear (#618); wordpress and discourse unchanged
#655 review: the sequence fetch moves clear of the hot-read floor (0.95 -> 1.6 calls/s) so seed jitter cannot move it in or out of the cache overlay; trailgear only

#653: a schema-qualified SQL Server reference ([Audit].[EventLog], or the three-part [db].[Audit].[EventLog]) resolves to its collected table id, so those queries are scored by their own table instead of the all-tables average; a name collected in two schemas is kept as written
#654: a tableless sequence fetch (SELECT NEXT VALUE FOR seq, Oracle seq.NEXTVAL FROM DUAL) is a utility statement kept on the chosen Aurora engine, and the cache overlay never fronts a sequence fetch
#663 (parser): a T-SQL MERGE names its target (and a USING table) and its WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET adds no table SET; a parameter like @From is never a FROM keyword
